statement: the pole that the Blaschke factor cancels sits at p = b = (d+1)/2 and has residue |S^d|/(2 zeta(d+1)): the volume term of a lattice of rank d+1 whose cusp has a horocycle of dimension d. At d = 1 it is 2/vol of the modular surface, recovering the classical Eisenstein residue 1/vol
consequence: the third entry of the dimension dictionary is not merely forced; it is a volume, and its coefficient is computable as one
scope: finite test cases; zeta is evaluated only at real arguments above 1, by a convergent series, and nothing here is a positivity certificate

groups.name: C. at d = 1 the residue is the volume of the modular surface

groups.note: residues in p are twice residues in s because 2s = p + b, so the classical Res_{s=1} phi(s) = 1/vol is recovered exactly
